summary: All three audio items are fixed and checked on my release build (Build/audio/PainterIO.exe). (1) robust-03 / perf-07: the three biome clip sets are now built at startup without blocking. The current biome's set is built synchronously as before. The two others are synthesized on worker threads (Task.Run) through a new additive interface ISplitSfxClipSet: Synthesize is pure C#, BuildSlot makes one AudioClip on the main thread. A new SfxClipSetLoader (in Sfx.cs) makes at most one clip per frame, and if the player picks a biome before its set is ready, Finish completes it at once. Build(rate) is now BuildSlot over Synthesize(rate) for all three sets, so both paths give the same samples (hash tested). Player check with a scripted click harness: the fire and electric sets were ready 2.12 s and 2.25 s after boot. The taps on Feu and Electricite logged no clip set build. The pre-fix build logged 'fire clip set built in 235 ms' and 'electric clip set built in 203 ms' on the same taps. (2) feel-04: the 8 clips that lost too much loudness through a phone speaker were reworked. Low voices are bent with an asymmetric tanh (drive 2.5), mid tick or splash layers were added, the lose jingle is doubled an octave up, and the Electricite hum was rebuilt as a 120 Hz buzz with 240-960 Hz partials. Now every one-shot loses at most 3.5 dB through the 400 Hz 24 dB/oct high-pass (before 13.1 dB) and the loops at most 5.1 dB (before 14.4 dB). Win and lose jingles are within 1.2 dB full range and 1.8 dB on a phone (before 9.4 dB). Fire fwump vs electric return distance is now 15.4 dB, or 14.6 dB after the high-pass (before 8.2). The other 22 clips are bit-identical to before (hash diff). (3) feel-13: when the human dies by territory loss, the 120 ms caught haptic now fires once through the same Pulse path as a spark death. A bot's elimination pulses nothing. Tests: 10 new WaveC_ tests. My filtered run (WaveC_Audio, SfxTests, FireBiomeTests) has 28/28 green. The latest full EditMode run on the shared tree (infra-perf, 16:49, after my edits) has 486 tests with 1 failure, which is another package's em-dash test. Sim unchanged: my build's probe gives PASS with hash 246577239DE179C4.

items.evidence: Code: ISfxClipSet.cs adds ISplitSfxClipSet (Synthesize(int) pure C# and thread-safe, BuildSlot(SfxClipSamples, SfxSlot) on the main thread), the SfxSlot enum and SfxClipSamples (raw float[] per slot, per-slot error strings, an FNV-1a Hash, CreateClip and MakeClip). The 25.2 interface is unchanged. LiquidSfx, FireSfx and ElectricSfx implement it, and Build(rate) is now BuildSlot over Synthesize(rate). The synthesizers were already pure C# with no UnityEngine call and no shared mutable static (only static readonly duration tables). The Debug.LogError calls moved out of the synthesis path into MakeClip, which runs on the main thread. Sfx.cs adds SfxClipSetLoader with Start (Task.Run), Step (at most one AudioClip per call), Finish (wait for the worker, then make the remaining clips), Abandon (Teardown destroys the clips already made), IsPending, SlotsBuilt and LastSamples. Sfx.BuildAudio builds the current set as before and then calls StartBackgroundSets. Tick calls UpdateBackgroundSets once per frame (not when hard-muted). SetFor finishes a pending set through loader.Finish and logs 'clip set was still loading when picked, finished in N ms'. The old synchronous 'clip set built in N ms' path remains only for the boot set or when no worker thread could start. Tests (TestResults/audio_edit1.xml, all green): WaveC_EverySetIsSplitAndItsWorkerSamplesHashLikeTheSynchronousGenerators, WaveC_SetsSynthesizedInParallelOnWorkersAreIdentical (6 workers at once, twice), WaveC_BackgroundBuiltFireAndElectricSetsHaveTheSamplesOfBuild (the loader pumped one Step per frame; names, lengths, rates and GetData hashes match a synchronous Build), WaveC_APendingSetPickedEarlyIsFinishedAtOnce. SfxTests and FireBiomeTests are green. Player (Build/audio, harness docs/waveC/audio/tools/biometap.ps1: windowed 540x960, -biome liquid -sfxlog, the window is focused at launch because runInBackground is false in the release player, then clicks on Feu, Electricite and Liquide; the game's PlayerPrefs are restored afterwards). docs/waveC/audio/biometap_after/p.log shows 'liquid clip set built in 82 ms' and '7/7 shared clips ... in 289 ms; 2 other clip sets synthesizing in the background'. It then shows 'fire clip set ready in the background (synthesized in 257 ms on a worker thread), 2.12 s after boot' and 'electric clip set ready in the background (synthesized in 234 ms on a worker thread), 2.25 s after boot'. Then come the three UiClick cues with 'bloom on (fire)' and no 'clip set built' line. Screenshots tap1_fire.png and tap2_electric.png (looked at) show the Feu and Electricite cards selected with the fire and electric attract behind. Baseline, same harness on the pre-fix Build/Windows (docs/waveC/audio/biometap_before/p.log): 'fire clip set built in 235 ms' right after the Feu tap and 'electric clip set built in 203 ms' after the Electricite tap. DevShot runs with sound on (-biome fire and -biome electric, -sfxlog): the other two sets were ready 2.37 to 2.71 s after boot, with no errors, no muted cue and a maximum output peak of 0.556. With -biome X at boot, X is the synchronously built set, so nothing is finished on demand. Shader warm-up stays deferred, as the plan says.

Re-run of docs/waveC/feel/tools/audio_analyze, compiled from the real sources. The copy is in my scratchpad, so no bin/obj was written to the tool's folder. Full output in docs/waveC/audio/audio_metrics_after.txt. An extended copy that also prints the acceptance summary and the band distances after the high-pass is in docs/waveC/audio/tools/audio_accept, with its output in docs/waveC/audio/audio_acceptance.txt. Phone loss in dB, before -> after: L.ReturnGloop 5.8 -> 3.5, L.CaughtSplat 6.8 -> 3.3, L.LoseJingle 8.8 -> 3.3, F.Pop 13.1 -> 3.2, F.Fwump 10.1 -> 3.1, F.Burst 5.6 -> 2.4, E.Return 8.9 -> 3.2, E.Ambient (loop) 14.4 -> 5.1. Maximum: one-shots 3.5 dB (limit 4), loops 5.1 dB (limit 6). Win vs lose jingle: play(L100+gain) -12.7 / -11.5 (1.2 dB apart, limit 3); phonePlay -13.1 / -14.8 (1.8 dB apart, before 9.4). F.Fwump vs E.Return 12-band profile distance: 15.4 dB (before 8.2), 14.6 dB after the 400 Hz high-pass (before 8.4), limit 12. Means used. SfxSynth gets AddDrivenVoice (asymmetric tanh, drive 2.5, bias 0.2), AddTicks and AddNoiseBurst. The gloop's bubbles are higher with stronger partials and its body is bent. The splat's body is bent and gets a 1.3 kHz splash burst, its noise floor goes from 300 to 650 Hz and its low-pass from 6 to 4 kHz, which keeps it dark. The lose jingle is G4 Eb4 C4 with 3rd partials, doubled an octave up with 4th partials; the G3 under the last note became a soft G4, the low-pass went to 4 kHz and the drive to 2.0. FireSfx: the pop has a bent thump, a 1.7 kHz burst and a 2.2 kHz tick layer. The fwump has a band-passed 520-1520 Hz whoomp, a bent 95-150 Hz tone, soft 1.8 kHz ticks and a 24 dB/oct 2.6 kHz low-pass (dark, no sparks). The burst has a bent boom, a 900 Hz noise floor and a 3 kHz tick layer. ElectricSfx: the return thunk is driven at 3.0 with a stronger rise, 4.8 kHz sparks and a 2.2 kHz contact click. The ambience is a 120 Hz buzz with 240/360/480/600 Hz and fainter 720-960 Hz partials, with spread phases so the loop point is not the steepest point (seam jump at the 45th percentile of steps, before 96th). It is still a 4 s seamless loop at peak 0.6. Constraints kept: lengths unchanged, peak 0.89 (0.60 for the ambience), one-shots start on silence and end on an exact zero, loops seamless, deterministic. These are now also locked by WaveC_EveryClipKeepsItsLoudnessThroughAPhoneSpeaker, WaveC_WinAndLoseJinglesAreEquallyLoudOnFullRangeAndOnAPhone, WaveC_FireFwumpAndElectricReturnStayDistinct and WaveC_EveryBiomeClipIsCleanAndEveryLoopJoinsSeamlessly (the same measure ported into the test). Only the 8 targeted clips changed: the per-clip sample hashes before and after (docs/waveC/audio/clip_hashes_before.txt and clip_hashes_after.txt) differ only for those 8. SfxTests and FireBiomeTests are green. Phone listening on a device is still pending for the gate (the 400 Hz model is a proxy).

Sfx.HandleEvent, Eliminated branch for the human: when the splat plays there (live and not already played on SparkCaught, which is the territory-loss death), Pulse(Haptics.CaughtMs) now fires through the same Pulse path that SparkCaught uses (Haptics.Pulse plus the HapticPulsed event). A spark death still pulses once, on SparkCaught. Contract 16 durations and createOneShot are unchanged. The Haptics.CaughtMs doc now says it also covers territory loss. Tests (green): WaveC_HumanTerritoryLostEliminationPulsesTheCaughtHapticOnce uses the RulesTests R9 scenario as a live GameSession with the human as the eliminated player 1: Cause TerritoryLost, pulses exactly [120], one splat. WaveC_BotTerritoryLostEliminationPulsesNothing: with the human as an idle third player, no pulse at all; with the human as the capturer, the 20 ms capture pulse and never 120. Sfx_DemoRoundPlaysTheHumanCuesAndHapticsInOrder is green with the same pulse list [20, 60, 40, 60, 120]. Feeling the vibration needs an Android device: pending for the gate.

api_additions: ISfxClipSet.cs: public interface ISplitSfxClipSet : ISfxClipSet { SfxClipSamples Synthesize(int sampleRate); void BuildSlot(SfxClipSamples samples, SfxSlot slot); } (additive; the 25.2 ISfxClipSet signature is unchanged)
ISfxClipSet.cs: public enum SfxSlot { Exit, Return, Fill, Cut, TensionLoop, Caught, LoopLost, Ambient }

ISfxClipSet.cs: public sealed class SfxClipSamples (SlotCount, Biome, SampleRate, SynthMilliseconds, Get/Set, ErrorOf/SetError, Hash(), static HashOf(float[], ulong), static CreateClip(name, samples, rate), MakeClip(slot, name))
Sfx.cs: public sealed class SfxClipSetLoader (Start(index, set, rate), Step(out index), Finish(index), Abandon(), IsPending, SlotsBuilt, AnyPending, LastSamples)
LiquidSfx: virtual Synthesize(int) / BuildSlot(...), static SfxId? LiquidId(SfxSlot), protected Assign(SfxSlot, AudioClip); the unused protected static Make(SfxId) was removed
FireSfx: Synthesize(int) / BuildSlot(...); ElectricSfx: overrides Synthesize / BuildSlot (Build is inherited from LiquidSfx)
contract_issues: 16 Haptics: 'caught 120 ms' also covers the human's elimination by territory loss (feel-13). A spark death pulses once on SparkCaught, a territory-loss death once on Eliminated.

25.2: the ISfxClipSet comment 'Sfx calls Build once, the first time the biome is used' is outdated. All three sets are now synthesized at startup: the current biome's set synchronously, the two others on worker threads through the additive ISplitSfxClipSet (Synthesize pure C# and thread-safe, BuildSlot on the main thread, one clip per frame), with SfxSlot and SfxClipSamples. Build(rate) equals BuildSlot over Synthesize(rate). A set picked before it is ready is finished at once. The 25.2 interface signature is unchanged.

16 / 25 (suggested binding budget, feel-04): every clip loses at most 4 dB (loops 6 dB) of K-weighted loudness over its loudest 100 ms through a 400 Hz 24 dB/oct high-pass (phone speaker model), and the win and lose jingles stay within 3 dB of each other on full range and on that model. WaveC_AudioTests enforces it.
25.4 'low hum ambience': the Electricite hum is now a 120 Hz buzz with 240 to 960 Hz partials (it was 50 Hz mains harmonics), so it is still a low hum but audible on phones.
open_issues: Side effect of the mid layers: the caught slot is 2 to 3 dB less distinct between biomes in the 12-band profile (L-F 13.7 -> 11.5, L-E 12.5 -> 9.8, F-E 10.9 -> 8.4). This is not an acceptance criterion and every pair is still at least 8 dB apart; it can be revisited if playtesters confuse the caught sounds.
E.Ambient is 1.6 dB quieter on full range (play -27.1 -> -28.7) but 7.7 dB louder on the phone model (phonePlay -41.4 -> -33.7).

Pending for the gate (needs a device): phone-speaker listening of the 8 reworked clips; the territory-loss vibration; worker-thread synthesis timing on an IL2CPP ARM64 phone (BuildAndroid was not run by this package; Task.Run is standard .NET and IL2CPP supports it).

Harness note: the release player has runInBackground false. A scripted player launch must focus the window, or the player pauses and the background sets wait until the first input. biometap.ps1 does this, and DevShot and probe set runInBackground themselves.

If a biome is picked in the first about 2 s after boot, before its set is ready, the rest is finished synchronously and logged ('clip set was still loading when picked, finished in N ms'). When only clip assembly remained, this was measured at 3 ms.

Full EditMode suite on the shared tree: the infra-perf run (16:49), the ui run (17:02), the actors run (17:06) and the biome-fire run (17:18, 487 tests, TestResults/biome-fire_edit.xml) all came after my last source edit (16:38). Each shows the 28 audio-owned tests (WaveC_AudioTests, SfxTests, FireBiomeTests) green and 1 failure, PainterIO.Tests.WaveC_BiomeFireTests.WaveC_FirePackageFilesHaveNoEmDash. That test file contains an em dash and belongs to biome-fire, not audio. On resume, the only source file changed after 17:18 was that biome-fire test file, so no new audio run was needed. PlayMode was not run by this package: no PlayMode test touches Sfx, and in batchmode Sfx is hard-muted, so the loader is never used there.
